articles.title: Trump heads to Iowa and Kansas with Senate control in balance
articles.summary: By Andrew Goudsward, David Morgan and Doina Chiacu WASHINGTON/ANCHORAGE, Alaska, Nov 1 (Reuters) - Two days before Tuesday's midterm elections, President Donald Trump's Republicans got an unexpected boost in Michigan with an endorsement from a prominent Democrat, while suffering a setback in Alaska when a federal judge dismissed a legal challenge. US Representative Haley Stevens, who lost Michigan Democrats' Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed in ‌a bitterly contested race, on Sunday publicly backed Republican candidate Mike Rogers, threatening to exacerbate divisions in a state viewed as crucial to Democratic hopes of retaking the US Senate. "I don't belong in Abdul's ‌campaign," Stevens said in a video posted to social media. Thirty-five Senate seats and all 435 House of Representatives seats are on the ballot on Tuesday. Republicans hold narrow majorities in both chambers. Polls show Democrats are favored to win a majority of the House and ​locked in a tight battle for control of the Senate with a handful of races likely to determine the outcome. The Trump administration's attempt to intervene in Alaska's Senate race faltered on Sunday when a federal judge dismissed the US Justice Department's lawsuit seeking to block certification of the results if Republican incumbent Senator Dan S. Sullivan narrowly loses. The Justice Department argued voters may be confused by the presence of a challenger named Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. on the same ballot. If Democrats take control of the House or Senate, they could block Trump's legislative agenda for his final two years in office and launch investigations of an administration that has so far faced largely compliant Republican majorities. The White House has ‌been preparing to implement portions of Trump's agenda without the aid of Congress. More ⁠than 52 million Americans have already voted in person or by mail, according to the University of Florida's Election Lab, a record for a midterm and up from nearly 46 million who voted before Election Day in 2022. MICHIGAN RIFT In Michigan, Stevens' endorsement of Rogers came on the same day she was supposed to appear with El-Sayed in a show ⁠of party unity. But the planned event unraveled after Stevens called on El-Sayed to condemn an outside group's ad that she said blames Israel for high grocery prices. "We can't stand with hate," Stevens told reporters on Sunday, standing alongside Rogers after joining him at a Detroit church service. El-Sayed's campaign recently asked Stevens to skip his events through Election Day so as "not to distract from the central issues of the campaign," a person familiar with the matter said. Republicans sought to take advantage of Stevens' move. "This is ​courage ​in politics in America today," Rogers said. "When you see a party, and at least a sliver of the party, veering off ​into the virulent hate that they have been spewing toward a group of people, it ‌gets dangerous." El-Sayed, who has been subjected to a campaign of racist and Islamophobic attacks, on Sunday declined to directly address Stevens' endorsement, saying he was focused on other issues. "I want to get money out of politics," El-Sayed told reporters. "I want to put money back in pockets." It was unclear whether the move would affect the outcome of the race. Polls indicate that El-Sayed has largely consolidated Democratic support. He holds a nearly 4-point lead against Rogers according to the Real Clear Polling estimate. ALASKA RULING In Alaska, a federal judge rejected a Trump administration lawsuit against the state. The DOJ had asked a court to block certification and order an investigation if the outcome indicated that voters may have voted for challenger Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. when they intended to vote for the incumbent Dan S. Sullivan. The issue has roiled the campaign over the last several days after the New York Times reported Democrat Mary ‌Peltola's campaign was involved in recruiting Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. into the race as a spoiler. The senator on Sunday said he ​would accept the results of Tuesday's election even as the Trump administration presses a criminal investigation into the issue. But Alaska Governor Mike Dunleavy, a ​Republican, has suggested he may not certify a victory by Peltola, and the incumbent Sullivan declined to ​say whether he would support efforts to refuse certification. He joined his party colleagues in accusing the other Sullivan of trying to confuse voters with his similar name. "They got the decoy ‌guy on the ballot," the senator told CNN's "State of the Union" program. "I'm sure I'm ​going to lose a lot of votes to that ​trickery. So what I say to Alaskans is, 'Don't let them get away with the tricks.'" Peltola has denied involvement, and Sullivan Jr. has denied coordinating with Peltola's campaign. TRUMP CAMPAIGNS IN RED STATES Trump is set to return to the campaign trail on Sunday with rallies in Iowa and Kansas, Republican-leaning Farm Belt states where his party is fighting to hold US Senate seats. Trump won Iowa by double digits in 2024. But ​polls show Democrats tied with or leading Republicans in many of the state's races. ‌And Trump's approval among rural Americans fell to a new low of 45% in October, according to Reuters/Ipsos polling. Kansas, which last elected a Democratic senator in 1932, is also facing an ​unexpectedly close race. (Reporting by Andrew Goudsward and David Morgan in Washington and Nathan Frandino in Anchorage; Additional reporting by Nathan Layne, Laura Matthews, Leah Douglas, Curtis Williams and Mike Scarcella; Writing ​by Brad Brooks and Andrew Goudsward; Editing by Lincoln Feast, Alex Richardson, Sergio Non, Will Dunham and Deepa Babington) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/trump-heads-iowa-kansas-rallies-110258414.html

articles.title: Democratic Senator Chris Murphy hospitalized after stroke, chief of staff says
articles.summary: U.S. Sen. Chris Murphy has been hospitalized after suffering a stroke, his chief of staff said in a statement on Sunday. The 53-year-old Democrat was taken to a hospital on Saturday after he started to feel numbness in his arm while attending his son's hockey game, said Allison Herwitt, Murphy's chief of staff. ABC News - PHOTO: Sen. Chris Murphy, pictured here in this appearance on ABC's "This Week," Feb. 9, 2025, was hospitalized, Oct. 31, 2026, after suffering a stroke, a top aide to the Connecticut Democrat said. Upon examining Murphy, doctors determined he had suffered a stroke, Herwitt said, adding that the senator has been transferred to Johns Hopkins Hospital in Baltimore. "The doctors are encouraged by his progress, he is awake and alert, and we are optimistic he will make a full recovery," Herwitt said. No further information was released about Murphy's condition. For the past several weeks, Murphy has been traveling the country campaigning for Democratic candidates in Tuesday's midterm elections. He was scheduled to appear Sunday with Democratic Senate candidate Chris Pappas in New Hampshire, according to the New Hampshire Democratic Party. Sen. Chris Murphy hospitalized after suffering a stroke, chief of staff says In 2024, Murphy won his third term to serve Connecticut in the U.S. Senate and has been viewed by some Democratic party officials as a possible candidate for president in 2028. Connecticut Gov. Ned Lamont released a statement on social media on Sunday saying he and his wife, Annie, are keeping Murphy and is family "in our prayers." "Just two days ago, I was with Senator Chris Murphy doing what he loves most: Encouraging Connecticut residents to make their voices heard and vote on Tuesday," Lamont said. "There is no stronger advocate for our democracy. And no one who fights harder for the people of this state. Chris is a great friend to Connecticut and to me personally." "I am sure that he will be walking across the state again very soon. And we will all be cheering him on," Lamont added. This is a developing story. Please check back for updates. articles.title: Judge dismisses DOJ lawsuit seeking to block Alaska Senate certification if GOP loses
articles.summary: A federal judge on Sunday dismissed the Justice Department’s lawsuit seeking to block certification of Alaska’s U.S. Senate race if Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan loses, two days before Election Day. U.S. District Judge Sharon Gleason wrote that the relief the government sought was “infeasible” because many ballots have already been cast and mixed together, the AP reported . She also wrote that the government “provides no workable plan” for separating ballots ranking Dan J. Sullivan and investigating them “in a manner that would preserve voter secrecy.” Gleason found the federal government did not have the ability to bring the case, NPR reported . Justice Department attorneys are expected to appeal, according to NPR. The ruling does not end the criminal investigation into how the second Sullivan got on the ballot. It was, for a while, considered one of those colorful quirks that crop up in the course of an election: the fact that not one but two candidates named Dan Sullivan will appear on the Nov. 3 ballot for U.S. senator from Alaska. One Dan Sullivan — Dan S. Sullivan — is the state's incumbent Republican senator. He is trying to fend off a fierce challenge from former Democratic Rep. Mary Peltola and secure a third term. The other Dan Sullivan — Dan J. Sullivan — is a retired teacher from a tiny fishing village along the Alaska Panhandle. He has never previously campaigned for public office, and he switched his registration from "unaffiliated" to "Republican " just before the deadline to run. (He has since switched back to unaffiliated .) But now the situation seems to be getting more serious. At President Trump's direction, the Justice Department sued last month in federal court to block certification of the election if Sen. Dan S. Sullivan loses, alleging that retired teacher Dan J. Sullivan is a Democratic plant whose purpose is to siphon away votes. Then, on Oct. 28, the New York Times published an extensive investigation that appears to substantiate that allegation , calling it "Democrats' secret effort to stack Alaska's ballot." "The Times has found, based on interviews and text messages, along with documents prepared for a potential lawsuit against the campaign, that not only did Ms. Peltola's team work with people trying to recruit Mr. Sullivan to run for Senate, but the effort was much broader," the paper wrote. "The group worked to coax other would-be spoilers into the race, to dilute the incumbent's support and help catapult the Democrat to victory." Matthew Salisbury, a former congressional candidate and Alaska insurance manager, told the Times that he was approached by a man claiming to represent wealthy donors who wanted him to run for Senate as an independent candidate. Salisbury said he met with the man over beers at an Irish pub in Anchorage, but ultimately declined after being unable to verify his identity. "I'm not naïve," he said. In response to the report, Trump called for both Peltola and the "fake" Dan Sullivan to be removed from the ballot in a post on Truth Social . Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy, a Republican, said he was ordering an investigation to determine whether the alleged effort violated state law. "Alaskans have a fundamental right to vote for the candidate they actually intend to support," Dunleavy said in a statement . "Deliberately tricking voters into casting their ballots for someone else strikes at the integrity of our elections." Sen. Lisa Murkowski, a Republican who has represented Alaska in the Senate since 2002, wrote in a statement that the people of her state deserve a full explanation. "Run and win on your merits: your views, your policy ideas, and your accomplishments," she wrote. "By contrast, recruiting candidates to manipulate the field and influence voting outcomes is simply wrong." Sam Curtis, a spokesperson for the Alaska Department of Law, told CNN that the revelations in the Times report did not change the state's opposition to a Trump administration lawsuit seeking to potentially delay certification of the election. "Placing candidates on the ballot is a matter of state law, not federal law," Curtis said, adding that the report has "no impact on the current litigation." Rep. James Comer, the Republican head of the House Oversight Committee, said Oct. 29 that the committee is "taking action" to launch an investigation into the matter, including an inquiry into whether any crimes may have been committed. ABC News also reported Oct. 29 that the DOJ had issued a wave of new subpoenas as it probes whether the alleged recruitment scheme may have run afoul of federal conspiracy laws. On Friday, Michael Heyman, the U.S. attorney for Alaska, confirmed there is a criminal investigation, saying it had been underway for months. He said the Times report led to a "significant surge of law enforcement assets" to the state, but declined to say what crimes are being examined and said he was "not making any assumptions on whether a crime has been committed," according to CBS News . Before the ruling, the Justice Department had also asked Gleason to order state officials to "preserve and segregate all ballots ranking Daniel J. Sullivan" so it could investigate possible voter confusion, and it requested action before Monday . State attorneys had asked the judge to dismiss the case, arguing that the ballot already distinguishes the two men. It lists the senator as Dan S. Sullivan, a Republican and the incumbent, and the challenger as Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., with no party, the AP reported . In a filing Saturday, Alaska's Republican-run government urged Gleason to dismiss the case, calling it a "meritless lawsuit" and the ballot request "both disturbing and impossible" because it couldn't be carried out without violating voter privacy, the AP reported . "Not every wrong can be righted in federal court," the state wrote. The Trump administration says it is trying to combat fraud. On Friday, a federal appeals court rejected a similar DOJ request in California to set aside disputed ballots. An FBI agent also visited the Petersburg business of a Sullivan donor to ask whether he had been misled, the AP reported . The donor said he hadn't. "Everybody knows who the incumbent is," he said. At a rally in Daytona Beach, Fla., on Friday, Trump said Peltola "should be removed from the ballot and prosecuted," adding that Attorney General Todd Blanche would make his own decision, MS NOW reported . No one has been charged. Peltola said at a rally in Anchorage that she was "so deeply offended by these accusations about having any involvement with anyone else's candidacy." Asked whether someone on her campaign could have been involved, she told KTUU, "I honestly have no idea." The Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee has denied involvement, and Dan J. Sullivan has long denied running at Democrats' behest. On CNN’s “State of the Union” on Sunday, Sen. Sullivan said he doubted Peltola’s denials. “There is no way this went on for a year that they weren’t informing her,” he said. Asked about certification, he said, “I’m going to accept the results of the election.” Sen. Tim Scott of South Carolina, who leads the GOP’s Senate campaign arm, said on NBC’s “Meet the Press” that criminal charges might make sense. Sen. Bernie Sanders, an independent of Vermont, said on CBS’ “Face the Nation” that what Democrats did “seems to me to be pretty dumb,” adding, “It’s not illegal.” Dunleavy, the Republican governor, suggested his state investigation could still affect the outcome. “If we find out there’s wrongdoing, and if that means that the certification then is stopped or changed, then that’s what happens,” he told NewsNation on Friday. The outcome of the fight could still have enormous national implications. Democrats need to win at least a few Senate races in historically Republican states to secure a majority in the chamber. Polls suggest Alaska is one of their best chances to turn a red seat blue. Given how close other races across the country appear to be, a move to block or erase a narrow Peltola victory could be the pivot point that allows the GOP to keep control of the Senate for the last two years of Trump's presidency. How did this happen, and where do things go from here? Here's everything you need to know to catch up and make sense of the story. How Alaska wound up with two Dan Sullivans on the ballot Ballot-stacking — the process of recruiting a spoiler candidate to help your candidate win — isn't unheard of in politics, and the Times says it's "generally considered legal." But it's a lot easier in Alaska than other states because of the unique way elections work there. When Peltola ran for reelection to the U.S. House in 2024, the state GOP backed an effort to help a second Democrat — an inmate who conducted his campaign from a New York prison — remain on the ballot. And during this year's primaries, super PACs aligned with both parties "flooded the state with ads for fringe candidates" in an attempt to "dilute support for the mainstream candidates opposed by the groups," according to an October Alaska Beacon report . How is any of this possible? The Last Frontier sends the top four primary candidates to the general election regardless of party — then asks voters to rank them on Election Day in order of preference. This means that candidates can claim any party affiliation on the ballot without being vetted by parties themselves. (Dan J. Sullivan initially claimed to be a Republican .) It also means that as long as they finish in the top four, primary candidates don't have to earn many votes to secure their very own ballot line on Nov. 3. (Dan J. Sullivan won 4,107 ). For months, Republicans have questioned Dan J. Sullivan's intentions and tried to get him tossed off the ballot. In June, the Alaska Supreme Court dismissed their arguments, ruling that neither state law nor the U.S. Constitution provided any legal basis for removing Dan J. Sullivan's name. How the Senate candidates will appear on Alaska's midterm ballot. elections.alaska.gov The more obscure Sullivan has "maintained that he [is] running in good faith and of his own volition, as a moderate Republican and not a secret Democrat," as a Times profile put it in August. He said he'd voted in the past for some Alaska Republicans, including Sen. Lisa Murkowski, even though he also "acknowledged previous donations to Ms. Peltola and a handful of other Democrats," and said he would prefer Peltola for Senate over the Republican incumbent "if it was between those two." But according to the Times report, "operatives aligned with" the Peltola campaign convinced Dan J. Sullivan to enter the race "to help Mary." The report cited as its sources 12 people "who participated in or were told of the plan" as well as interviews with other would-be recruits and dozens of internal text messages. For the record, both Peltola's campaign and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, which directs the party's campaign strategy in Senate races across the country, have denied any "involvement," and Dan J. Sullivan did not respond to the Times's repeated requests for comment. One of the Times's main sources — former Peltola campaign manager and longtime aide Elisa Rios, who had been planning to file a wrongful termination lawsuit — also tried to retract her statements to the paper ahead of publication. The Times story described an elaborate endeavor — which was "internally called the ballot composition project" — that "involved secret trips to far-flung Alaskan communities and the appearance of a mysterious Midwestern operative, who traversed the state using a fake name and made his pitch to would-be candidates over beers at brew pubs." The Times also reported that the "Peltola campaign's lawyers, as well as senior aides at the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee" were "involved" with the effort. The Trump administration's lawsuit Legal battles over the dual Dan Sullivan issue had been confined to state courts until last month. That's when Trump's administration filed its lawsuit aiming to have the certification of the results blocked if Peltola wins a close election that may have been affected by Dan J. Sullivan's presence on the ballot. "Should Alaska certify any electoral results tainted by the inclusion on the ballot of Daniel J. Sullivan … the State and its officers will fail in its obligation to protect the integrity of its election," the Department of Justice wrote in its legal filing. "I'm the one that said do it," Trump said last month of the lawsuit. The suit argued that a Democratic victory should be considered invalid if Peltola wins by a margin smaller than the total number of votes that Dan J. Sullivan receives — under the assumption that those votes may have come from confused voters who intended to vote for the incumbent Republican senator instead. Democrats asked the courts to dismiss the lawsuit, arguing that the administration lacks "any statutory or constitutional authority to insert itself" into the state's electoral process. Alaska's state government, which is currently led by Republicans, also moved to dismiss the administration's lawsuit. On Oct. 26, a federal judge agreed to fast-track consideration of the dispute to potentially allow it to be resolved before Election Day. Before Gleason's ruling, many legal experts said the lawsuit had a slim chance of success. First, it required a very specific outcome in which Peltola wins by what would likely need to be a very thin margin. Even in that scenario, election law experts said, the appearance of confusion on the part of voters did not create legal grounds for the federal DOJ to have the results rejected. "I believe that this lawsuit is abusive in its intentions and borders on frivolous in its arguments, and that it is destined for defeat in the courts should it reach the merits," Walter Olson, a senior fellow at the Cato Institute, a libertarian think tank, told the Alaska Beacon . Nicholas Stephanopoulos, a Harvard law professor, told the Harvard Gazette that the law the administration is relying on in its lawsuit — the National Voter Registration Act (NVRA) — does not give federal authorities any power to challenge state election procedures. "The lawsuit has nothing to do with voter registration. There's no allegation that anybody is improperly registered in Alaska; there's no claim that Alaska isn't in compliance with the NVRA's requirements for voter registration," Stephanopoulos said. More generally, experts say the lawsuit runs against the Constitution's language granting states the power to run their own elections. "This is purely a matter of state law, and the administration has absolutely no authority to tell Alaska when or how to certify the results of its Senate election," David Becker, a former Justice Department attorney who worked on voting rights cases, told Alaska Public Media . What's next? Voters decide the race Tuesday. The Justice Department is expected to appeal Gleason’s ruling, while the federal criminal investigation, Dunleavy’s state investigation and the House Oversight Committee’s inquiry continue. An appeal would likely only matter in an extremely close race, which is not the recent norm in Alaska. The last time Dan S. Sullivan was on the ballot, he defeated his top challenger, independent candidate Al Gross, by 45,000 votes . The most recent Senate race, in 2022, was closer, but the top two finishers were both Republicans. Things are expected to be much tighter this time around. Peltola has held a consistent lead in the polls since the summer, but her advantage has steadily shrunk in the months leading up to Election Day. The most recent surveys have her ahead by 2 points, well within the margin for Sullivan to win. The Cook Political Report, one of the nation's most respected election forecasters, lists the race as a toss-up. Another well-regarded forecaster, the Center for Politics, categorizes it as "leans Democrat." articles.title: At 11th hour, Dem Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers in Mich. Senate race
articles.summary: DETROIT (AP) — Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed’s former opponent in the U.S. Senate primary , Haley Stevens, stunned party officials Sunday by endorsing Republican Mike Rogers as Democratic tensions boiled over days before the election that could determine the balance of power on Capitol Hill. Stevens endorsed Rogers after attending a Detroit church service with him. The remarkable show of support for the President Donald Trump-backed candidate in the tightly contested race comes after she was uninvited to a joint event the same day with El-Sayed, who defeated the congresswoman by a slim margin in the August primary. “Our Democratic nominee for Senate said I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away," Stevens said in a video announcing the endorsement, which led her top aide to quit. “And he's right. And that's why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today.” El-Sayed dismissed the endorsement when asked about it by reporters later Sunday, saying he's focused on issues voters care about, such as the high cost of living. “At the end of the day I actually don’t think about Haley Stevens," he said, adding later: “None of this matters." Michigan Democratic leaders were left shocked. With just less than 48 hours to go before Election Day, a party that had spent months trying to unite behind its Senate nominee was suddenly grappling with an extraordinary defection in one of this year's most important races. Tensions between the two Democrats have festered since the primary. Stevens is a staunch supporter of Israel, while El-Sayed is a fierce critic of the U.S. ally. He has also been criticized by some in the community for past remarks regarding a Michigan synagogue attack and for appearances with controversial streamer Hasan Piker . El-Sayed, a former Michigan public health official, is facing Rogers, an ex-congressman, for the seat held by the retiring Democrat, Gary Peters. Keeping Michigan in Democratic hands is vital to the party’s effort to win a majority for the final two years of Trump’s second term. Stevens and El-Sayed were originally scheduled to attend church together, along with other Michigan and national Democrats, including South Carolina Rep. Jim Clyburn. Democrats hoped it would be a show of unity as they worked to boost turnout in the Detroit area, where concerns have lingered about enthusiasm among Black and Jewish voters in key Democratic strongholds. Instead, Stevens swayed to gospel music alongside Rogers in the pews at Perfecting Church, while El-Sayed was a few miles away at a different house of worship campaigning alongside prominent Democrats, including Clyburn. The Associated Press attended both services as the dramatic split-screen unfolded. Stevens' team resigns as Democrats are stunned by reversal After the church service north of Detroit, where Stevens and her fiance Jason Turkish worshipped with Rogers and his wife, Kristi, the congresswoman told reporters, “I’m not turning my back on Democrats. It is this one vote.” Rogers, standing beside her, said he was “honored” by her support. Their appearance came days after Stevens publicly reaffirmed she would vote for her party's nominee. It also led her longtime chief of staff to resign, with a number of staff members expected to follow soon, according to a person familiar with the developments who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss internal matters. “We are shocked and heartbroken,” the aide said in a statement. The state party chair, Curtis Hertel, said Stevens' endorsement “shows that she has abandoned everything she claims to care about.” “We reject the attempts by Stevens and bad-faith actors to divide our party and undermine our momentum," Hertel wrote, and won't let such 11th-hour “distractions” deter the campaign. Hertel later wrote that Stevens "is not a current member of the Michigan Democratic Party, nor will she be in the future." Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, who supported Stevens in the primary, denounced her endorsement of Rogers. “This is a despicable betrayal from Rep. Stevens,” Schumer wrote in a social media post. Dingell says she disinvited Stevens after it became ‘distracting’ Among the Democrats who joined El-Sayed at church Sunday morning were U.S. Rep. Debbie Dingell of Michigan, U.S. Sen. Angela Alsobrooks of Maryland and state Sen. Mallory McMorrow, who dropped out of the Senate primary before voting began. Dingell, a senior Democratic figure in the state who helped organize the planned joint appearance, said she asked Stevens not to attend and that Stevens told her she would abide by that. “I'm the one who pulled it, because it had become way too distracting," Dingell said in an interview before Stevens appeared with Rogers. “This is not how I was going to spend my weekend before the election, to be perfectly frank.” In the August primary, Stevens defeated El-Sayed in Wayne County, which includes Detroit, and neighboring Oakland County, drawing support from Black and Jewish voters who are important parts of the Democratic coalition. Early voting for Tuesday's election has been underway since Oct. 24. As of Friday, more than 1.8 million people had already voted in Michigan. How did we get here? The Democratic primary was among the most bitter this year. Each candidate accused the other of making personal attacks. Tens of millions of dollars in outside spending poured into the race, including from the American Israel Public Affairs Committee’s affiliated super PAC, which backed Stevens. El-Sayed took particular offense to an outside group’s ad accusing him of disrespecting women. Although Stevens pledged after the primary to help El-Sayed however she could, the two have not appeared together publicly since a unity breakfast two days after his primary win. Last week Stevens’ fiance told The Detroit News that he would vote for Rogers. Stevens later appeared on CNN to reaffirm her support for El-Sayed but urged his campaign to “shut out the hate and call it out.” But on Friday, after The Associated Press reported on the planned joint appearance, Stevens released a lengthy statement calling on El-Sayed to condemn an ad by an independent left-wing group that linked U.S. support for Israel to high grocery prices. “Abdul promises to get money out of politics,” Stevens wrote. “He can begin by getting Israel out of his explanation for everything Michigan cannot afford.” El-Sayed responded: “So while Congresswoman Stevens seems intent on relitigating a primary that ended three months ago, let’s all focus on the task at hand.” He made clear the ad was not made by his campaign and said “I do not agree with the contents of that ad.” Trump and Republicans revel in the discord Trump praised Stevens in a Truth Social post, saying she was “a Highly Respected Democrat” and that her support from Black and Jewish voters in Michigan is “virtually unprecedented.” “Haley said what few people are willing to say. She showed great and almost unprecedented loyalty to the Great People of Michigan with what she did,” Trump wrote. “It’s a thing called bravery, and few people have it like just displayed by Congresswoman Haley Stevens!” Appearing with Trump in Iowa for a campaign rally, House Speaker Mike Johnson said that he spoke to Stevens after she endorsed Rogers. Johnson said he “encouraged her to stay safe and keep speaking the truth.” A spokesman for the Republican National Committee, Hunter Lovell, said Democrats who feel abandoned by El-Sayed “have a home” with Rogers. ___ Cappelletti reported from Washington. These atmospheric rivers often fuel heavy rain events in the West, especially in a stronger El Niño winter. We'll discuss more about this pattern after laying out the important forecast details. articles.title: Pete Hegseth is facing a new threat — and it's not just from Democrats
articles.summary: Earlier this year, Senate Republicans decided to tighten the screws on Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The Pentagon had, for months, stonewalled lawmakers' request for materials related to the military's deadly targeting of alleged drug traffickers in Latin America. So this spring, the GOP-led Senate Armed Services Committee made a threat: grant access to the documents or it would block one of the Trump administration's political nominees. Subscribe to The Post Most newsletter for the most important and interesting stories from The Washington Post. Hegseth relented, said two people familiar with the exchange, speaking like some others on the condition of anonymity to discuss private conversations and the secretary's standing with Congress. Spokespeople for the committee and the Pentagon declined to address questions about the episode. The standoff, which has not been previously reported, illustrates Hegseth's increasing susceptibility to congressional oversight and how he might attempt to navigate a shift in the balance of power on Capitol Hill should Democrats prevail in this week's midterm elections. With limited exception, Republican lawmakers have declined to stand in Hegseth's way while he has purged dozens of senior military leaders he's deemed disloyal, waged an eight-month war in Iran without the consent of Congress and pursued an unprecedented campaign against the illicit drug trade. Democrats would give Hegseth far less room for maneuver once the next Congress convenes in January. Already, some are threatening to investigate and try to remove him from office if they reclaim a majority. Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said in a statement that, "despite threats of sham witch hunts," Hegseth is "100% committed" to leading the Defense Department "until the end" of President Donald Trump's term and to advancing the president's agenda for the military. The secretary "will not back down or be deterred by politicians seeking to score partisan points or launch phony investigations where no wrongdoing exists," Parnell said, adding that the department under Hegseth "has followed the law." Rep. Adam Smith (Washington), the top Democrat on the House Armed Services Committee, said in an interview that, as chairman, he would probe three areas: military operations, politicization of the armed forces and potential corruption in the Pentagon's awarding of defense contracts. The Defense Department is readying for such inquires. Those preparations include accounting for the likelihood that if Democrats take charge they will summon military officers to testify on Capitol Hill, people familiar with the matter said. Hegseth faces a more imminent challenge, though. When lawmakers return to Washington later this month, the House will probably vote on an effort to impeach him over the Iran war. That effort is being led by Republican Rep. Thomas Massie (Kentucky), a frequent critic of the administration. "There's a decent chance that it could pass the House, and I think that would be a stain on his record," Massie said in an interview. "If he's contemplating leaving, this would be a good time to do it." The House vote is expected to be close, but the effort is highly unlikely to result in a conviction if it advances to the Senate for a trial. Some officials in the administration and in Congress have mused recently that Hegseth may leave the Pentagon if Republicans lose heavily in the midterms - either to avoid congressional scrutiny or to pursue potential political ambitions. It's possible, too, that the president could remove Hegseth if voters punish the GOP over the Iran war, though Trump has said he stands by him. Two people familiar with Hegseth's thinking said the secretary wants to stay in office for four years. One said it's "silly" to think Democrats having greater control on Capitol Hill will change that. The other person said that Hegseth's September address to hundreds of service members in Quantico, Virginia, was meant to be a road map for his next two years in office, including priorities such as building a new U.S. military base and adopting advanced weaponry. An impeachment would be difficult for Hegseth if he does not stay in office, with significant legal costs and less control over what the Defense Department provides to congressional investigators, another person said. Asked by a reporter Thursday about the prospect of an impeachment, Trump - twice impeached himself - called the threat against Hegseth "terrible" and repeated his confidence in the secretary. "He's a great warrior," the president said. Some Democrats acknowledged being concerned that, should they regain a majority in Congress, repeatedly targeting Hegseth could imperil their ability to compromise with Republicans on critical defense legislation. Still, many of those who sit on the committees that oversee the Pentagon say that Hegseth hasn't worked with them for his two years in office. "Since I became ranking member, I have had the cellphone number of every single secretary of defense," said Smith, who has held the prominent House role for nearly 16 years. "Hegseth does not speak to me." Others in the party have vowed to oust Hegseth. Rep. Jason Crow (D-Colorado), told reporters in October that he would do "everything possible" to remove Hegseth if Democrats retake the House. Hegseth's defenders say they loathe the thought of Trump giving the Democrats "a scalp" by forcing him out, one administration official said. With the president's support, Hegseth has survived multiple controversies, including his use of the commercial messaging app Signal to share highly sensitive details on an imminent military strike and the military's decision to kill two people who survived a strike on an alleged drug boat. But in recent weeks, members of both parties have grown more willing to confront Hegseth, signaling they will block his preferred choices to lead the Army and denouncing his call to live-stream the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan, who committed a mass killing at Fort Hood in Texas in 2009. Current and former officials familiar with the Pentagon's standing on Capitol Hill said that Hegseth's challenge after the midterms will be to shore up bipartisan support for the military and defend his record as lawmakers from both parties have grown more critical of him. Two of the officials asserted that Hegseth could work across party lines, depending on how aggressive Democrats were in their investigations. Still, several others predicted that his critics, both in Congress and in the Pentagon, could feel more emboldened to oppose him if Democrats take power. "Pete has made so many enemies - and uncontrollable enemies," one person familiar said. articles.title: Shootings across 5 states leave 6 dead and at least 36 injured over Halloween weekend
articles.summary: Dozens of people were injured and at least six people died in mass shootings as gun violence broke out at nightlife districts in half a dozen cities across the country over the Halloween weekend. Police in Dallas, the site of the deadliest violence, said four people are dead and 15 others were injured following a handful of shootings in the city's Deep Ellum neighborhood, a center of music, restaurants and nightlife in the city. Police in college towns like Fayetteville, Arkansas; Birmingham, Alabama; Newark, Delaware, and Bloomington, Illinois, also reported shootings in their nightlife districts this weekend. Dallas Police Chief Daniel Comeaux said investigators are still trying to determine if the shootings Saturday night over the span of about an hour and 15 minutes were related. Comeaux said three separate shootings occurred, and it wasn't immediately known why they started. Comeaux said some arrests were made but he didn’t specify how many or what charges were involved. “This is a really big scene. It's spread out,” Comeaux said. “We are interviewing some individuals right now that we have arrested, still trying to figure out exactly how it ties into all the shootings out here.” The department had increased police presence in the district before the shootings. No police officers were injured. One shooting happened after an HBCU football game In Birmingham, Alabama, one person was killed and eight others were wounded in a mass shooting just outside Legion Field after the annual ‘Magic City Classic’ football game on Saturday night, police said. Michael Pickett, chief of the Birmingham Police Department, said most spectators and families had left the stadium property after the game, but the shooting happened nearby, where vendors were set up along Graymont Avenue. He said he was “very grateful that more people weren’t injured.” The circumstances of the shooting were unclear. Police spokesperson De'Rell Freeman said one person had been detained and transported to police headquarters for questioning, and “multiple weapons” had been found and secured. Alabama State and Alabama A&M are historically Black universities and archrivals whose annual contest has been played for more than 100 years. Nearly 70,000 fans attended Saturday's game, won by Alabama A&M 31-28. The event draws some of the largest crowds in the country for games played in their college football division. The Magic City Classic has such a deep history that Alabama State coach Eddie Robinson Jr., a former NFL linebacker and alumnus of the school, proposed creating a Hall of Fame for the game. In Newark, Delaware, six people were shot late Saturday near the University of Delaware campus, Newark police Lt. Greg D’Elia said. All six were transported to hospitals for treatment, police said early Sunday. No updates on their condition were available as of Sunday afternoon. A university spokesperson said they would provide updates on the investigation online as they become available. Video shared on social media showed people running for safety from the scene. One stretch of the city's Main Street was closed for several hours after the shooting, police said. A shooting early Sunday in Bloomington, Illinois, left a 19-year-old woman dead and another woman in critical condition. Six others had injuries that were not life-threatening, but it was unclear from a statement by the city's police department and McLean County Coroner’s Office if those people had gunshot wounds. The shooting happened near the campus of Illinois Wesleyan University. Bloomington is about 135 miles (217 kilometers) southwest of Chicago. Two shootings occurred in Arkansas A shooting early Sunday near a strip mall southwest of Little Rock, Arkansas, left one man dead and “several more” injured, city police said on Facebook. Police didn't specify the exact number of injured. And in Fayetteville, Arkansas, six people were taken to hospitals with gunshot wounds from a shooting that happened early Sunday. No arrests have been made, police said in a news release. A preliminary investigation indicates an altercation preceded the shooting. Halloween stores were the scene of two attacks On Friday, two people were killed in separate shootings at Spirit Halloween stores in California and Michigan. Police said a shooting inside a store at an indoor shopping mall in Fairfield, California was a targeted attack. Family members told police that the 31-year-old woman who died was pregnant. Six other people were wounded, police said. In Madison Heights, Michigan, just north of Detroit, a 21-year-old man was fatally shot Friday afternoon at a Spirit Halloween. Another man who was assaulted by bystanders as officers took him into custody was hospitalized with injuries that were not life-threatening, police said. ___ Raby reported from Charleston, West Virginia. AP reporters Claudia Lauer in Philadelphia and Laura Turbay in Little Rock, Arkansas, contributed to this report. articles.title: AI stocks just lost $5 trillion — but the stock market's sweetest stretch might be now
articles.summary: The AI trade just had its scariest October in years. The rest of the stock market barely noticed. The biggest AI and chip stocks have shed about $5 trillion in market value since Oct. 6, by Yahoo Finance calculations. Nvidia ( NVDA ) and Alphabet ( GOOGL ) have each given up roughly $835 billion in market cap, and Intel ( INTC ) lost nearly half its value in October. Everything else? The other 625 large US stocks in that tally added about $1.3 trillion. And while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) slipped this week, 9 of its 11 sectors rose about 1% or more, something that hadn’t happened in any week since at least 1999, by Yahoo Finance calculations. Yahoo Finance Jeff Hirsch, editor of the Stock Trader's Almanac , has a name for this: "Octoberphobia." And he's buying the sell-off. "I did buy some today... this is an opportunity here," Hirsch told Yahoo Finance on Friday . "The damage isn't as bad as the headlines are." Hirsch also has the calendar on his side. October selloffs like this one often lead into what the Almanac calls the sweet spot of the presidential election cycle , which runs from the fourth quarter of a midterm year through the following June. History is on the buyers' side From the last October close of a midterm year to the end of the following June, the S&P 500 has risen 19 times out of 19 since 1950 , with a median gain of about 15%. Chip stocks have been 8-for-8 since 1994, with a median gain of about 22%. Yahoo Finance The ride wasn't always smooth. Chips fell another 11% or so before turning higher in 2002 and 2018, and eight cycles is a relatively small sample. Chips just sprang a possible bear trap The iShares Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ) tumbled about 17% in October, yet it's still up more than 50% this year. On Friday, it dipped as low as $460, below the $464 low from July 29 that marked this summer's bottom. Then it closed at $472, back above that line. That's the look of a bear trap — a breakdown that reverses, catching traders betting on more losses. Chip stocks briefly broke below their July low Friday, then closed back above it. Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace Hirsch likes the timing. "Historically, seasonally, it sets up great for this period of time, the best months of the year for semiconductors," he said. His firm placed a new buy in the sector on Friday. Bulls first need to reclaim about $524, the top of last week's bounce, then the early-October high near $596. Losing the July low would put the February-April range near $370 in play. That's about 21% below Friday's close. The case for waiting Not everyone is loading up the shopping cart. BofA's Michael Hartnett said it's "risk-off until global rate hike ends," pointing to 42 central bank rate hikes worldwide over the past six months. The Fed held on Wednesday , but two officials voted to hike. Hartnett's line in the sand for chips is $520 on the VanEck Semiconductor ETF ( SMH ), which closed Friday near $522. On SOXX, that works out to about $469, just above the July low it barely held. So the bulls' and bears' lines sit almost on top of each other. Hirsch said he'd change his view on a decisive break of the S&P 500's mid-September low near 7,550, less than 1% below Friday's close. Tuesday's midterm vote comes first. Then November, the S&P 500's best month of the year , gets its turn. Internal AI tools helped analyze interview transcripts, research, and draft this post. Humans reviewed, edited, and fact-checked this post before publication. Jared Blikre is the global markets and data editor for Yahoo Finance. articles.title: Trump calls $50 million contract for ex-lawyer Habba Mildon 'not acceptable'
articles.summary: By Gram Slattery and Jasper Ward PALM BEACH, Oct 31 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump said on Saturday it was "unacceptable" for one of his ‌former lawyers, Alina Habba Mildon, to secure a $50 million contract for ‌herself while working at the US Department of Justice. "I thought it was totally obnoxious and outrageous, ​and it's not acceptable," Trump told reporters at his Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida. "Not acceptable at all." The New York Times reported last week that the family of Julio Herrera Velutini, a Venezuelan banker facing US felony bribery charges before ‌striking a plea deal in ⁠August 2025, guaranteed Habba Mildon more than $50 million over four years. The deal, according to the newspaper, would pay $10 million a ⁠year plus bonuses. Trump said he told Habba Mildon he did not want her to be paid and called the episode "terrible." Habba Mildon was serving as the acting US attorney ​in New ​Jersey when she signed the contract with ​Herrera's family company, Concord Partners, ‌days after it was registered in late October 2025, the New York Times reported. By the time she started her employment with the Herrera family, a court had disqualified her from serving as US attorney. She resigned on December 8 and was appointed a senior adviser to the attorney general the same day, ‌and was still in that role when, ​according to the New York Times, she started ​at Concord on January 1. Trump ​pardoned Herrera on January 15, 2026, according to the Justice ‌Department's website. Habba Mildon last week said ​she was never paid ​for a pardon, never met with anyone at the White House or Justice Department about a pardon, and never did any work for ​a pardon for anyone. The ‌Justice Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment. (Reporting by ​Gram Slattery in Palm Beach and Jasper Ward in Washington; ​Editing by Sergio Non and Lincoln Feast.) articles.title: McDonald's must face lawsuit alleging McRib contains no rib meat
articles.summary: A federal judge on Friday allowed a lawsuit against McDonald's to move forward, alleging the fast food chain misleads customers into believing its popular McRib sandwich contains actual pork rib meat. File Photo by Stephen Shaver/UPI Oct. 31 (UPI) -- A federal judge on Friday allowed a lawsuit against McDonald's to move forward, alleging the fast food chain misleads customers into believing its popular McRib sandwich contains actual pork rib meat. McDonald's had asked the court to dismiss a lawsuit in Chicago alleging consumer deception, fraud and unjust enrichment. But U.S. District Judge April Perry ruled the lawsuit, filed by four customers in December 2025, could move forward, FOX Business reported. First sold in 1981, the McRib features a boneless pork patty molded to resemble ribs. It is covered in barbecue sauce and served with onions and pickles. The plaintiffs accuse McDonald's of using the sandwich's name and appearance to suggest that it contains rib meat, despite allegedly using cheaper portions of pork. The lawsuit claims the McRib is made from ground pork products, including shoulder, heart, tripe and stomach, rather than meat taken from the ribs, according to KTLA . McDonald's has denied the allegations. One survey submitted in the case found that 72% of respondents believed the sandwich contained pork rib meat. Another survey found 67% considered rib meat an important factor in their decision to buy the McRib. The ruling comes as McDonald's brings back the McRib for another limited run. The sandwich returned to participating restaurants Oct. 27 in locations including Los Angeles, Chicago, Miami, Dallas, Atlanta and Philadelphia. 单季新增577亿美元，增速毫无放缓迹象 为精确呈现第三季度的变化，可将已提交三季报的五家公司与其二季度数据进行对比。这五家公司的合并表外承诺从2.48万亿美元增至3.05万亿美元， 单季增幅5770亿美元，增幅23%。 各公司具体情况如下： Meta新增1950亿美元，增幅29%。 亚马逊新增1310亿美元，增幅41%， 为超大规模云企业中百分比涨幅最大。无条件采购义务几乎翻倍，从1300亿美元增至2540亿美元，新增一项1596亿美元的"物业及设备"条目；尚未启用租约从1370亿美元增至1650亿美元。唯一抵消项是向OpenAI尚欠的213亿美元已于三季度入账，转移至资产负债表。受资本支出超预期冲击，亚马逊股价上周五大跌。 Alphabet新增1640亿美元，增幅18%。 采购承诺上升950亿美元，尚未启用租约从850亿增至1310亿美元，能源设备担保（期限延伸至2049年）从76亿美元翻倍至162亿美元，并新增一项66亿美元的TPU硬件回购担保。Alphabet在此前已向股权市场融资800亿美元、自由现金流持续告负的背景下，其表外承诺已突破1万亿美元大关，成为首家单一公司表外承诺超过1万亿美元的企业，达到10590亿美元。 微软新增350亿美元，增幅6%， 是其中表外承诺扩张相对"克制"的一家。三季度新签数据中心租约约530亿美元，其中170亿美元已启用并转入资产负债表，尚未启用租约从3290亿美元增至3650亿美元。需注意的是，微软的采购和建设承诺每年仅在10-K中披露一次，目前的2290亿美元数据仍停留在6月末，实际数字届时大概率将大幅上修。即便如此，"最干净"的超大规模云企业近期仍需发行250亿美元债券融资。 SpaceX新增510亿美元，增幅174%， 增速最为激进。其表外承诺从二季度末的290亿美元增至三季度末的400亿美元，再到10月26日通过8-K文件披露的400亿美元Apollo GPU主融资租赁协议（租赁期定于2027年上半年开始执行）后，总规模跃升至800亿美元。 评级机构口径不一，市场开始自行定价 高盛的Amanda Lynam指出，若将五家主要超大规模云企业的表外租约与采购承诺合并统计，相关规模自2023年以来已增长八倍。然而，这一风险敞口在评级体系中并未获得统一对待：标普在计算杠杆时对表外租赁进行调整，而穆迪与惠誉则未做同等处理，评级方法论的潜在变化因此成为值得密切追踪的风险点。 这种会计处理上的不透明，已开始引发市场的直接反应。分析机构Needham指出，一旦将表外负债纳入计算，Meta的企业价值将提升35%。Meta在财报披露后CDS创下历史新高，随即宣布大规模股权融资。Lynam亦强调，部分企业已明确表示需要在市场趋于饱和之前提前锁定资本，这一表述被认为是Meta股权融资的直接注脚，且未必是最后一例。 表外承诺扩张的三大构成 从结构上拆解这4.1万亿美元，可见三条主线： 一是尚未启用的已签署租约，总规模已达1.39万亿美元， 较8月时的1.12万亿美元进一步扩大。这些资产通常由特殊目的载体（SPV）出资建设的数据中心外壳构成，只有在正式通电启用后，才会转入公司资产负债表。 二是采购承诺，规模为2.25万亿美元， 较8月末的1.73万亿美元大幅攀升。这一类别包含了Meta斥巨资锁定的第三方云计算容量、亚马逊新增的物业设备采购义务等。 三是担保与兜底承诺，已从1580亿美元跃升至2730亿美元， 包括Alphabet的能源设备担保及TPU硬件回购担保，以及Meta在两个数据中心合资项目上的剩余价值担保。 表外债务扩张，市值同步蒸发 摩根士丹利曾于8月警告，这些承诺在算力供应受约束期间具有"战略价值"，但"若供需在预期之前趋于正常化，企业将不得不为过剩产能买单，或试图重新谈判合同条款"。 市场已开始给出答案。Alphabet股价本月经历创纪录的单日暴跌，亚马逊持续走低，纳斯达克100指数成份股本月合计市值蒸发逾1.2万亿美元。 换言之，一个季度内，大型科技公司新增约1万亿美元表外负债；一个月内，这些公司的市值缩水同样超过1万亿美元。表外承诺不因股价涨跌而消失，到期必须兑付。当前的核心悬念在于：AI商业化收入能否在下一轮承诺浪潮到来之前实现追赶——而下一个10-Q季报季，距今并不遥远。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 存储是“科技避风港”？野村：估值只有2-3倍了
articles.summary: 科技巨头AI军备竞赛持续升温，自由现金流加速恶化，而存储芯片制造商却在悄然积累现金。野村证券认为，当前市场对存储板块的定价存在根本性误判。 据追风交易台消息，五大科技公司三季度财报相继出炉，AI投资意愿不减反增，但各公司资金实力开始出现分化。Meta单季度自由现金流首次自IPO以来转负，录得-21亿美元；Alphabet连续两个季度为负，达-91亿美元；Amazon滚动12个月自由现金流缺口扩大至-424亿美元。与此同时，存储芯片厂商现金持续积累，据野村估算， 以三星电子和SK海力士为代表的韩国存储"双雄"2027年预期市盈率仅约2-3倍，较科技巨头折价85-90%。 野村在10月30日发布的报告中指出，市场当前对存储板块的定价隐含着盈利见顶的假设，但该机构对此判断明确持异议。报告认为， 存储供应短缺将延续至2028年，长期供应协议亦在增加，存储制造商的大规模股东回报周期才刚刚开始，在科技板块整体承压的背景下，存储是更值得关注的"避风港"。 AI投资意志坚定，但资金耐力开始分化 野村报告显示，企业级AI投资已演变为一种生存性需求，各公司正动用经营性现金流、债务与股权多渠道筹资。三季度中，仅Microsoft自由现金流保持正值，录得+186亿美元；Alphabet已于今年6月宣布800亿美元股权融资并暂停回购；Meta发行无投票权C类新股，同样叫停回购；Amazon年内长期债务规模升至约1075亿美元。资本市场的反应直接反映了投资者的偏好——现金流为正的Microsoft股价基本持平，而Meta、Alphabet、Amazon在财报发布后分别下跌7%、10-13%和5-7%。 在2027年资本支出层面，五家公司均未给出具体数字，但均明确表示将继续增加。野村援引SK海力士的数据称，2027年全球云服务商资本支出增幅有望达60%，对应四大超大规模云厂商合计支出约1.2万亿美元，远超市场一致预期的30-35%增幅。野村估算显示，若按60%增速情景测算，四家公司2027年合并自由现金流将转负至-1440亿美元，资金缺口须以债务和股权融资填补，资本将更加向融资能力强的企业集中。 云业务盈利改善，但现有业务遭AI蚕食 三季度，Azure、Google Cloud和AWS三大云平台合计营收同比增长56%，达1099亿美元，在手订单积压高达1.82万亿美元。AWS和Google Cloud的运营利润率分别达38.7%和36.2%，盈利能力持续改善。野村测算，在每GW资本支出500亿美元、年收入190亿美元的基准假设下，云数据中心IRR约为6-15%；若按当前现货租赁价格（每GW每年400亿美元）测算，IRR可升至13-31%。 然而，AI对现有业务的蚕食效应已开始显现。Google搜索收入增速从二季度的17%放缓至三季度的12%，查询量增长创五年新高，但Google自身的AI模式正在摊薄每次查询的变现效率。野村指出，这表明AI投资已不仅是增长工具，更是保护现有业务的防御性手段——即便是投入最重的Google，也无法独善其身。 三季度资本支出不及预期，折射供给瓶颈而非意愿退缩 Microsoft、Alphabet和Meta三季度资本支出均低于市场预期。Microsoft实际支出为452亿美元，低于公司自身指引的500亿美元以上，原因是第三方数据中心产能交付延迟，部分支出推迟至2027年上半年；此外，微软调整建筑物使用寿命的会计处理方式，将新增租约归入经营性租赁，导致报告资本支出数字下降，但实际支出计划不变。Alphabet和Meta均未解释差距原因，Amazon则明确将芯片（晶圆代工）供应不足列为瓶颈。野村认为，随着2027年供应短缺加剧，意图与执行之间的时滞将进一步扩大，成为新常态。 Intel业绩承压，PC市场下行压力超出市场预期 Intel四季度营收指引为150-160亿美元，低于市场预期的约170亿美元，财报发布后盘后股价下跌21%。野村指出，PC市场下行是行业普遍问题：内存价格上涨与供应短缺导致三季度全球PC出货量同比下降约20%。Intel自身亦面临公司特有挑战，包括Intel 3制程及基板供应短缺、以色列工厂事故导致四季度及下一季度服务器出货量各减少约3亿美元，以及PC产能难以快速向服务器转移等结构性制约。与此同时，AMD在服务器和PC市场均在持续抢占份额，Arm阵营（包括NVIDIA Grace/Vera、AWS Graviton、Google Axion等）亦在侵蚀Intel的服务器CPU市场。 现金流两极分化，存储估值被严重压低 野村报告的核心论点在于：科技巨头与存储制造商之间正在形成截然相反的现金流走势。科技巨头的自由现金流理论上将经历"J曲线"——前期重资产投入完成后，大量经营性现金流将随之而来。但目前来看，负自由现金流局面才刚刚开始，且未来一两年内缺口可能进一步扩大。 反观存储制造商，大规模股东回报的起点同样才刚刚到来。 野村预计，未来数年内存储厂商的股东回报将成倍增长，在可观股东回报之后现金储备仍将大幅提升。当前市场却给予存储板块2-3倍的2027年预期市盈率，而四大科技巨头平均约为20.9倍（Microsoft 24.3倍、Amazon 21.7-23.3倍、Alphabet 18.5倍、Meta 18.1倍），折价幅度达85-90%。 野村认为，当前估值隐含着存储盈利已见顶的假设，但鉴于供应短缺将持续至2028年、长期供应协议持续增加，市场对存储盈利持续性的判断过于悲观，存储板块构成当前科技组合中难得的"避风港"。 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ 以上精彩内容来自 追风交易台 。 更详细的解读，包括实时解读、一线研究等内容，请加入【 追风交易台▪年度会员 】 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 华尔街大佬：亚马逊、微软和Meta，越跌越买
articles.summary: 潘兴广场资本管理创始人、CEO Bill Ackman表示，他已逆势买入因巨额资本开支承诺而遭市场抛售的亚马逊、Meta和微软，目前三家公司合计占其投资组合约三分之一。

articles.title: 何处是底
articles.summary: 摘要 1 拐点的出现：海外科技巨头的投资回报再度受到市场的审视 从本周美股云厂商财报来看，AI相关投入持续高企，但盈利与现金流的兑现速度仍难以匹配资本开支的扩张幅度，未来投资回报与融资可持续性并未获得明确保证。当前云业务收入的持续增长意味着AI投入正在转化为可量化的投资回报，符合预期；但与此同时，新世界与旧世界的矛盾也在激化，谷歌广告与亚马逊电商收入增速均边际下行，在新业务的发展尚不足以带来充裕现金流的同时，传统业务增长动能的走弱则削弱了当下云厂商依靠内部现金流支撑巨额资本开支的能力。而从债务与收入的视角来看，随着云厂商外部融资规模的扩张，利息支出也开始对利润产生一定的侵蚀，典型的如亚马逊利息支出占净利润比重由25年平均3%提升至26Q3的8.2%。尽管新业务确实在增长，但传统业务受损叠加利息负担加重，反而使得谷歌和亚马逊自由现金流出现大幅回落，这也意味着当下云厂商仍难以形成“云业务增长→现金流修复→资本开支扩张”的正向循环。财报披露后各家云厂商不同的业绩表现也使得股价表现存在差异，微软因能够实现正自由现金流而获得市场的“奖励”，财报披露后EPS上调且股价上涨；而亚马逊、谷歌则因业绩miss（财报披露后EPS下调）、现金流骤降而出现股价大跌。目前看，对美债利率而言，随着一致预期中2026Q4的AI资本开支放缓，美债利率的顶部可能已经出现，但考虑到当下美国经济基本面仍具备韧性，未来美债利率的下行幅度则仍有待观测，利率的快速下行仍需要等待AI融资出现快速收缩的下一个路标信号。 2 科技调整的幅度观测：2007周期股VS2026的硬件科技 从两个维度来看科技调整的幅度：（1）此前我们中期策略提出本轮AI产业周期可类比于2005-2007年中国的制造业投资周期。对比2007-2008年周期股与本轮科技股股价的回撤有相似之处：本轮科技股自7月初调整以来回撤幅度约54%，出现在美国科技股只是上行逆转但未出现明显调整之前；2007-2008年美股见顶并未出现次贷危机前，中国周期股于2007年10月见顶至2008年6月回撤幅度为62%。但值得关注的是，2008年美股真正的加速下跌是在2008年8月之后，彼时则对应次贷危机风险升级、产业链量价齐跌；与此同时，A股也未能幸免，2008年8月之后全A仍有40%以上的跌幅，相关周期板块跌幅也接近50%。当下来看，中国AI硬件相关资产是美国上游供应商，和中国在2007年加入WTO后是美国需求供给方有类似，后续需要密切关注美国科技与债务周期情况。目前来看，尽管云厂商模式的可持续性仍有担忧，但AI商业化路径确实正在体现，仍在分歧时期。（2）从市场交易指标来看：①两融担保比例本周继续回落；②主要宽基指数隐含波动率上行，当前科创50、创业板指、中证1000的隐含波动率均已升至3年90%以上的分位数水平，但上述两个指标距离历史极值仍有一定距离。③市场宽度来看，A股整体与科技股内部均已降至历史低位。当前交易结构确实已经开始具备底部条件，但交易指标距离历史极值还有一定距离则意味着倘若尾部风险出现，相关指标向历史极值靠拢仍有可能给市场带来下行风险。值得一提的是，当前AI硬件超配比例仍高于大多历史主流赛道超配比例的峰值，主动偏股基金对AI硬件整体的持仓暴露依然较高。结论是，按照历史极端行情看，当下并不具备抄底条件。如果交易指标进一步出现极端值且配合美股的企稳，可能才是阶段性反弹的时机。 3 盈利下行时期：应对市场波动的结构性线索 当前企业盈利的周期性放缓开始体现在经济数据和企业财报当中：今年6月以来工业企业利润增速连续4个月边际回落，与此同时上市公司2026Q3利润端开始出现降温迹象。结构上，以盈利正增长占比所衡量的盈利扩散度在2021年以来仅高于22Q4，景气依然稀缺，利润增长主要集中于少数高景气行业。值得关注的是，尽管非科技领域整体盈利有所放缓，但部分行业的景气韧性仍在，与其在科技板块的高波动中反复博弈，不如将视野拓展至非科技领域，财报视角下可关注高景气延续组合（共12个行业如煤炭开采）和困境反转组合（共7个行业如炼化及贸易）。 4 为未来的行情积蓄力量 尽管价值投资者应该在“他人恐惧时贪婪”，但判断何时是真正的“恐惧”是最大的难度。作为这轮参与全球产业链映射的中国投资者而言，国内市场的下跌幅度本身并不是衡量“恐惧”最好的尺度，这也是抄底过程中最大的陷阱。在美国科技巨头资本开支拐点出现后，我们对未来1-2年资本成本的回落、科技应用的开花与中国资产的崛起充满信心，现在我们将致力于等到这天的出现。我们推荐：第一，以煤炭、石油、油运为代表的能源链将继续受益于全球对能源的补库需求，能源链是资本成本波动与地缘冲突下的韧性资产；第二，财报视角下建议关注：①高景气延续：医疗服务、专业连锁、煤炭开采、航运港口，以及有色、化工中的细分领域等；②困境反转策略：纺织服装的细分领域，以及造纸、炼化及贸易、医疗器械等。第三，黄金在实际利率拐头时期可能会受到流动性冲击，但参考2008年经验大的机会也在因此孕育。 风险提示：国内经济修复不及预期；海外经济大幅下行。 报告正文 1 拐点初现：海外科技巨头的投资回报再度受到市场的审视 随着科技行情行至下半场，当前市场对AI的关注也正在转向投资回报的验证阶段，然而从本周美股云厂商财报来看，目前并未给市场提交一份令人满意的答卷：AI相关投入持续高企，但盈利与现金流的兑现速度仍难以匹配资本开支的扩张幅度，“造血”能力尚未跟上“烧钱”的速度，未来投资回报和融资可持续并未获得明确的保证。从云厂商本身的业务收入来看，2026Q3亚马逊AWS、谷歌Cloud和微软Azure收入分别实现39.3%、102.6%和48.2%的同比增速，需求仍在高速增长，AI投入正在转化为可量化的投资回报，也符合预期；但与此同时，新世界与旧世界的矛盾也在激化，云厂商传统业务的受损正在体现在财务报表当中，其中谷歌的广告业务、亚马逊的在线商店收入增速边际下行（2026Q3同比分别为10.6%和1.6%），在新业务的发展尚不足以带来充裕现金流的同时（2026Q3微软、谷歌、亚马逊云业务占整体收入比重分别为36%、24%、23%），传统业务增长动能的边际走弱在带来业绩miss的同时也削弱了云厂商依靠内部现金流支撑巨额资本开支的能力。 从债务与收入的视角来看，自从去年四季度开始云厂商转为依赖外部融资之后，当下云厂商在长期借款出现明显增加的同时（尤其是亚马逊和谷歌），利息支出也开始对利润产生一定的侵蚀，例如2025年亚马逊利息支出占净利润比重平均约为3%左右，但2026年以来逐季增加，2026Q2开始达到8.2%。而相比之下，“优等生”微软在保持相对债务融资相对克制的同时其利息支出占净利润的比重则维持相对稳定的水平。尽管新业务确实在增长（对应的也是AI商业化路径正在得到验证），但传统业务受损叠加外部融资增加后所带来的利息负担加重，反而使得巨额资本开支下2026Q3部分云厂商的自由现金流出现大幅回落，这也意味着当下云厂商仍尚未形成“云业务增长→现金流修复→资本开支扩张”的正向循环。值得一提的是，财报披露后各家云厂商不同的业绩表现也使得股价表现存在差异，微软因能够实现正自由现金流而获得市场的“奖励”，财报披露后EPS上调且股价上涨；而亚马逊、谷歌则因业绩miss（财报披露后EPS下调）、现金流骤降而出现股价大跌。 对美债利率而言，过去AI投资的持续扩张支撑了美债利率的上行，然而当下云厂商的盈利模式尚未形成闭环，尽管资本开支仍在增加，但未来增速放缓的拐点可能已经出现。随着市场对前期AI产业乐观预期的修正，美债利率的顶部可能已经出现。但考虑到当前美国经济基本面仍具韧性，2026Q3美国GDP超预期，投资侧依然对美国经济形成支撑，同时AI投资向其他领域的扩散也还在持续，未来美债利率的下行幅度则仍有待观测，这是我们前面几期周报讲到的最青黄不接的时候。 2  当前A股科技股的位置 从海内外的科技股表现来看，尽管美股以费半为代表的AI硬件在上半周出现企稳，但随着云厂商财报披露，市场再度出现反复波动；与此同时，本周A股科技股板块也出现明显回调。实际上，自从今年6月底以来，A股电子、通信为代表的科技股回撤幅度已达甚至超过50%。而站在当前时点来看，在股价经历显著回调、AI产业的可持续性仍处于验证期的背景下，目前A股科技股已经回落至什么位置，以及前期调整是否已释放相关风险则正在成为市场关注的核心问题。 2.1 类比2007-2008年周期股的下跌 此前我们在中期策略报告中曾指出本轮AI产业周期来看，真实的盈利、随处可见的短缺与通胀、以及投资预期占全球GDP比例抬升的程度，与当年中国加入WTO后的中国制造业投资中的周期牛市存在诸多相似之处。而参考2005-2007年行情周期见顶的原因，并非是单纯的资金面破灭所致，而是金融条件、产业链利润分配格局以及外部宏观环境多方因素的共振。对比2007-2008年周期股与本轮科技股股价的回撤有相似之处：本轮科技股自7月初调整以来回撤幅度约54%，出现在美国科技股只是上行逆转但未出现明显调整之前；2007-2008年美股见顶并未出现次贷危机前，中国周期股于2007年10月见顶至2008年6月回撤幅度为62%。而从股价和估值的调整节奏来看，本轮科技股的下跌斜率明显更为陡峭，市场对产业预期的修正与估值收缩的速度也更快。 值得关注的是，从2008年美股的表现来看，美股真正的加速下跌实际上是在2008年下半年。2007Q2之后全球GDP已经陷入增长瓶颈，而大宗商品价格仍在上涨，产业链陷入“价升量减”的不稳定状态，类似于经济周期中的“滞胀”状态，市场开始定价盈利下修的风险。而随着2008年6月雷曼提前透露第二财季可能出现亏损，尤其是8月房利美、房地美相继披露二季度亏损，市场对金融体系风险的担忧逐步升温；尤其是在9月雷曼破产之后流动性冲击与资产抛售则使得美股开始出现快速下跌。与此同时，A股也未能幸免，全球金融危机爆发、外需走弱的冲击下，2008年8月至11月万得全A仍有40%以上的跌幅，周期股跌幅则接近50%。当下来看，中国AI硬件相关资产是美国上游供应商，和中国在2007年加入WTO后是美国需求供给方有类似，后续需要密切关注美国科技与债务周期情况。目前来看，尽管云厂商尚未形成盈利的正向循环，AI产业链未来投资回报与融资可持续性仍有待验证，但云业务的增长也说明AI商业化路径正在逐步验证，仍在分歧时期。 2.2 交易指标已符合底部区域，但距离历史极值仍有距离 上周周报中我们提出观察市场位置的两个交易指标：融资融券担保比例和宽基指数期权隐含波动率。而从最新情况来看：①融资融券担保比例截至周四数据为250%，倘若考虑周五的调整后（以万得全A周五跌幅2.34%测算）可能进一步回落至244%左右。目前3年分位数、回撤、去杠杆均满足我们上周周报所提及的底部条件，交易结构已得到一定的出清。不过，倘若与历史极端水平进行对比，如24年1月的220%、25年4月的240%，当前两融的担保比例距离历史极值仍有一定的距离。②本周主要宽基指数的隐含波动率均出现上行，尤其是科创50、创业板指、中证1000的隐含波动率均已上升至近三年90%以上的分位数水平，交易情绪逐步接近底部区域。不过，与两融担保比例相类似，当前隐含波动率距离历史极值也还有一定差距。③此外，从市场宽度来看，无论是A股整体还是科技板块内部，当前市场宽度均已降至历史低位，尤其是以电子、通信为代表的科技板块，市场宽度已创下年内新低。因此，当前交易结构确实已经开始具备底部条件，但交易指标距离历史极值还有一定的距离则意味着倘若尾部风险出现，相关指标仍可能向历史极值靠拢，市场也不排除存在下行风险的可能。 值得一提的是，从筹码结构来看，目前依然出清较为缓慢，2026Q3主动偏股基金对于AI硬件(光模块、PCB、半导体等)的配置比例/超配比例快速回落至45.2%/26.4%，但无论是与AI硬件自身比、还是对比历史其他主流赛道资产，主动偏股基金对于AI硬件的配置/超配比例依然处于历史高位，值得一提的是，当前AI硬件的超配比例仍高于大多历史主流赛道超配比例的峰值。即虽然三季度AI硬件遭遇较大的回撤，但主动偏股基金对于AI硬件的减持幅度较为有限，整体的持仓暴露依然较高。 3  盈利下行时期：应对市场波动的结构性线索 当前企业盈利的周期性放缓开始体现在经济数据和企业财报当中：自今年6月以来工业企业利润总额累计增速已连续4个月下滑，与此同时上市公司盈利在经历2025年以来的持续修复之后，2026Q3利润端开始出现降温迹象，全A（非金融地产）的归母净利润整体/扣非口径下分别相较Q2边际回落4.3/1.9个百分点至11.2%/11.3%。结构上，以盈利正增长占比所衡量的盈利扩散度在2021年以来仅高于22Q4，景气依然稀缺，利润增长仍主要集中于少数高景气行业，尚未形成广泛的盈利扩散。 值得关注的是，尽管相比科技的高增长，非科技领域整体盈利有所放缓，但随着海外AI投资回报的可持续再度受到审视，与其在科技板块的高波动中反复博弈，不如将视野拓展至非科技领域，部分行业的景气韧性可能使得相关板块具备性价比，或将是配置结构再平衡中值得关注的重要线索。而从财报视角下，我们主要从两条思路进行筛选： （1）高景气延续：从业绩增速绝对值视角下，2026Q3营业收入与归母净利润单季度增速排名均处于前30的二级行业，包括：有色金属（小金属、能源金属、工业金属）、医药生物（医疗服务）、商贸零售（专业连锁）、煤炭（煤炭开采）、交通运输（航运港口）、基础化工（化学原料、化学纤维、非金属材料）、机械设备（自动化设备）等。 （2）困境反转：边际视角来看，我们设定连续两个季度营收增速、归母净利润增速与ROE（TTM）边际改善作为景气度持续性回升的判断依据（如果已入选高景气延续组合则从困境反转组合中剔除），最终筛选出来的行业包括：有色金属（金属新材料）、轻工制造（造纸）、石油石化（炼化及贸易）、建筑装饰（装修装饰）、纺织服装（纺织制造、纺织家纺）、医药生物（医疗器械）等。 4  为未来的行情积蓄力量 尽管价值投资者应该在“他人恐惧时贪婪”，但判断何时是真正的“恐惧”是最大的难度。作为这轮参与全球产业链映射的中国投资者而言，国内市场的下跌幅度本身并不是衡量“恐惧”最好的尺度，这也是抄底过程中最大的陷阱。在美国科技巨头资本开支拐点出现后，我们对未来1-2年资本成本的回落、科技应用的开花与中国资产的崛起充满信心，现在我们将致力于等到这天的出现。基于以上内容，我们推荐： 第一，以煤炭、石油、油运为代表的能源链将继续受益于全球对能源的补库需求，同时也是资本成本高位震荡+地缘冲突下的稳定资产； 第二，财报视角下建议关注：①高景气延续：医疗服务、专业连锁、煤炭开采、航运港口，以及有色、化工中的细分领域等；②困境反转策略：纺织服装的细分领域，以及造纸、炼化及贸易、医疗器械等。 第三，对于黄金而言，实际利率下行前半段可能会受到流动性冲击，可以等待时机。 风险提示 国内经济修复不及预期：如果后续国内经济数据超预期走弱，那么可能会对长期盈利趋势的改善造成影响。 海外经济大幅下行：如果海外经济超预期下行，那么全球制造业共振修复可能会暂停，实物资产需求也会放缓。 本文来源： 一凌策略研究 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 一生难愈：高盛发现被AI取代的工人通常再就业困难，且往往落入AI的下一个猎场
articles.summary: 被人工智能淘汰的工人，正在陷入一场难以自救的循环。高盛最新研究显示， AI冲击劳动力市场的迹象已从科技行业蔓延至金融、保险、房地产和专业服务等更广泛领域，而失业工人不仅比其他被裁员者更难找到新工作，重新就业后往往又落入AI下一轮替代的射程之内。 高盛经济学家Pierfrancesco Mei在最新报告中写道，在非制造业领域，AI采用率较高的行业如今已呈现出更弱的就业增长和更高的失业率。数据显示，被AI高度暴露岗位淘汰的工人，再就业平均需要多花约一个月时间，且在失业一年后仍处于失业状态的概率比其他被裁员者高出约10个百分点。 与此同时，高盛首席经济学家Jan Hatzius指出，每提升10个百分点的AI采用率，对应行业的就业增长将减弱约0.9个百分点，失业率将上升约0.9个百分点。 更令人担忧的是， 这场冲击的全面爆发或许尚未到来。高盛经济学家Joseph Briggs警告，历史规律表明自动化裁员往往集中于经济衰退期，当前企业在盈利繁荣期选择暂缓裁员，一旦经济下行，多年积压的AI替代性裁员可能在同一时间集中释放，与周期性失业叠加共振。 AI就业冲击：从科技蔓延至主流行业 此前，市场对AI取代就业的担忧曾被普遍质疑。Apollo分析师Torsten Slok在今年8月表示，AI对就业的冲击"微不足道"，其研究发现AI主要压缩的是薪资而非岗位数量——AI暴露度最高岗位的薪资增速，在2023年后比低暴露岗位慢6.7%，但就业人数并未出现统计意义上的显著变化。 然而，高盛的最新数据呈现出明显的转折。Mei利用美国人口普查局"流离失所工人补充调查"的新数据，覆盖2016年至2025年逾15000名非自愿失业工人，将其中2023至2025年的最新队列界定为"首批AI替代工人"。通过综合职业AI暴露度、行业AI采用率及岗位消除方式构建的复合评分，高盛将最可能因AI而失业的前30%工人单独提取，与其他被裁员者进行比对。 结果显示，2024年以前差异并不明显，但2025年出现清晰断层： AI替代工人的再就业时间明显拉长，长期失业概率显著上升。高盛指出，这一短期冲击幅度"与过去历次技术变革浪潮对失业工人的影响相当"，意味着"AI只会创造就业、不会消灭就业"的论断已难以为继。 入职即入坑：再就业者频陷AI下一轮替代 高盛研究中最令人不安的发现，并非失业时间的延长，而是再就业的方向。 在以往的技术变革中，被技术淘汰的工人往往"向下流动"，转入更为程式化、复杂度更低的岗位，其原有技能随技术迭代逐步贬值。 当前的AI替代浪潮呈现出类似甚至更为严峻的模式。 AI替代工人在再就业时，倾向于寻找能沿用既有技能的岗位，但这恰恰使他们更易暴露于下一轮自动化风险之中。 高盛数据显示，AI替代工人再就业后落入同等或更高AI暴露岗位的概率，从2018年至2023年约55%的中位水平，跳升至2024年的约65%，并在2025年进一步攀升至近75%。 换言之，四分之三被AI淘汰的工人，正在走回AI的下一个猎场。 美国劳工统计局的数据同样印证了这一趋势：2023至2025年间，共有740万工人非自愿失业，高于上一调查周期的630万；而在找到新全职工作的长期失业者中，薪资达到或超过原岗位水平的比例仅约49%，较两年前的约62%大幅下滑。 疤痕效应：损伤随年龄加深，代际差距显现 高盛历史数据显示，技术性失业的影响具有长期性。 在失业后数年间，技术替代工人的实际薪资增速持续低于其他被裁员者，再次陷入失业的概率也长期偏高。在过去四十年的个体数据中，年龄偏大、无大学学历、居住在农村以及在原岗位任职时间较长的工人，其失业十年后的累计实际薪资差距约为8至10个百分点，约为年轻、受过大学教育、城市居住及短期任职工人的两倍。 不过，高盛在新数据中发现一处相对积极的信号：年轻工人对AI冲击的适应能力明显更强。2025年，35岁以下的AI替代工人重返全职工作所需时间，比其他失业者约多三周；而35岁及以上者则多出约五周，且经历了更多临时性工作和兼职的过渡阶段。 高盛还注意到，在校大学生"正日益选择AI暴露度较低的专业"。然而，斯坦福数字经济实验室的数据显示，22至25岁从事AI高度暴露职业的年轻人，就业水平已较正常情形低约19%——其困境并非适应速度慢，而是根本无人招聘。 大规模裁员待发：衰退或成引爆点 当前美国失业率仍处于4.2%的相对低位，AI替代效应尚未在宏观数据中充分显现。 高盛经济学家Briggs的解释是：历史上，常规岗位自动化带来的就业冲击绝大多数集中于经济衰退期。 数据显示，从事常规岗位的美国工人比例在每一轮经济扩张期基本持平，随后在1980年代初、2001年、2008年和2020年经济下行时呈台阶式下跌，且从未反弹。 Briggs基于三种历史推算方法得出，技术进步每带动劳动生产率提升1%，将在峰值时推高失业率约0.3至0.4个百分点，且以岗位消失为主要驱动。以高盛对AI最终将提升15%生产率的预测为基础，估算显示最终将有约9%的工人在AI过渡期间被替代，另有3%的额外雇用萎缩压力，合计约1500万美国工人——高于年初6%至7%的估算。 Briggs明确指出，企业在经济景气时倾向于保留冗余岗位，一旦经济转向，便会借助周期性下行的掩护集中推进自动化。更令人警觉的是，AI资本支出热潮本身已成为当前经济增长的重要支柱，而Hatzius警告这一动能正在见顶—— 这意味着触发下一轮衰退的导火索，或许正是AI本身。 美国银行经济学家则持相对温和立场，认为"AI对劳动力市场的影响在2026年前可能仍相对有限，更广泛的结构性重组更可能在2027年发生"。即便如此， 这一"乐观情形"也仅将大规模冲击推迟约两年。 采用率仍低，影响却已显现 值得关注的是，高盛指出目前仅有约23%的美国企业将AI纳入部分常规工作流程，且这一数字"高估了当前实际发生的自动化程度"。 然而，就是在这一相对有限的采用率下，AI已在科技行业以外产生统计显著的就业损失，而失业工人再就业后又大概率再度暴露于AI替代风险之中。 如果AI采用率从现有水平翻倍乃至翻三倍，上述每一项效应都将进一步放大：追逐有限"AI难以替代"岗位的失业工人增多，失业时间进一步拉长，转入新岗位的工人面临二次替代。Briggs的结论是，这一冲击的主体部分很可能在下一轮衰退到来时集中释放，恰恰是经济最缺乏消化能力的时刻。 Briggs警告，美联储及其他央行"应密切关注任何新出现的下行增长或劳动力市场风险"，一旦近期通胀约束解除，"迅速转向宽松可能有助于确保自动化相关失业不会在经济最脆弱时加速爆发"。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 谁能阻止科技股下跌？野村：中选没有用，只有美联储！
articles.summary: 全球科技股深陷调整泥潭，市场普遍寄望于美国中期选举后的政策明朗化带来反弹契机，但野村证券策略师Naka Matsuzawa泼了一盆冷水。他明确指出， 中期选举结果对股市的影响远低于市场预期，当前唯一能够真正终结科技股跌势的催化剂，是美联储停止加息。 Matsuzawa在10月30日的宏观策略周报中预判，11月2日中选当周，美股将偏软，债市将偏强，美元偏弱，日元偏强。他认为， 科技股的疲弱根源并不在于选举不确定性，而在于AI投资前景承压与信贷担忧持续发酵这两条更深层的主线。在这一背景下，半导体股的短暂反弹既缺乏持续性，也缺乏广度，难以带动全球科技板块整体回升。 中期选举的市场影响被高估 市场主流预期认为，若民主党同时赢得众参两院选举，美股将下跌、债市将上涨、美元将走弱，原因在于市场担忧财政政策陷入僵局以及AI相关监管趋严（包括对数据中心建设的限制）。 然而，Matsuzawa对此持怀疑态度。 他指出两点关键证据：其一，期货等市场中围绕中期选举的事件溢价已经明显下降；其二，预计受更严监管冲击的公司股票并未出现明显跑输市场的迹象。换言之，当前科技股的下跌并不一定与监管收紧的担忧直接挂钩，选举本身可能并非金融市场的核心驱动力。 他由此得出结论：选举结束并不能消散笼罩科技股的不确定性，那些押注选举过后股市反弹的投资者，其预期大概率将落空。 科技板块内部轮动，问题比表面更深 过去一周，科技板块内部出现明显分化。自7月以来领跌的半导体股出现反弹，而此前相对抗跌的超大规模云计算（hyperscaler）及软件股则回落。 Matsuzawa认为，这不能简单定性为板块内部的资金轮动，背后有更深层的逻辑需要厘清。 投资者当前呈现出两个明显倾向： 一是对核心业务营收和盈利的超预期结果并不特别买账，但对于不及预期则反应严苛；二是相比激进的资本支出计划，市场更青睐克制投资、改善现金流、提升股东回报的策略。这折射出市场对AI投资大幅放缓风险的深层担忧。 半导体股方面，美股半导体指数SOX本周大涨6.9%，日韩半导体股也尚未真正走出调整。资本品与机械股——通常是AI投资复苏预期的先行指标——同样未见起色，进一步表明市场对AI投资前景的信心并未实质性改善。 信贷担忧与美联储加息：牵动全局的两根主线 债市层面，本周出现一个耐人寻味的现象：信贷担忧虽有所缓解，但美国长端利率下行，而日本和德国长端利率反而上行。 Matsuzawa将这一分化归因于各大央行政策会议结果相对于市场预期的鹰鸽差异。 美联储此次表态较市场预期偏鸽，承认金融条件已趋于收紧；欧洲央行同样承认金融条件收紧，但明确发出12月加息信号；日本央行则未提及金融条件收紧，明确表示底层通胀已达2%，并上调了通胀预测。 对于本周公司信贷担忧缓解的原因，Matsuzawa提出两种解读： 一是主要由美国加息预期下降驱动；二是科技公司财报及IPO前景改善了市场对其融资能力的信心。鉴于超大规模云计算股本周表现疲弱，他倾向于前者解读。若下周美国就业报告超预期，则将推升美联储加息预期，并可能重新激化信贷担忧，局面将更趋复杂。 美元与日元：信贷情绪主导，加息预期退居次席 外汇市场方面，本周美元走强，日元承压，美元/日元下探157.5至158.0区间。这一走势在一定程度上令人意外——美国加息预期下降，通常应对美元构成压力，但信贷担忧缓解带动半导体股和银行股反弹，支撑了美国股市的相对表现，吸引此前出走的资金回流美元资产。 Matsuzawa警示，若半导体股和银行股的反弹缺乏持续性，加息预期下降的逻辑将重新占据主导，届时美元将面临较大的下行压力。 在日元方面，截至10月20日的投机性外汇持仓数据显示，日元多头有所增加，但目前仓位规模仍仅相当于2025年4月美国关税冲击期间峰值的39%，意味着日元多头仍有较大增仓空间。 只有美联储停止加息，才能打破僵局 Matsuzawa明确指出，当前很难找到能够将全球科技股从低迷中拯救出来的催化剂。选举结果、板块轮动、个别财报——这些因素均不足以从根本上改变科技股的运行逻辑。 他在报告中写道， 目前能够识别出的最重要潜在催化剂，是美联储加息周期的终结。在这一前提实现之前，科技股将持续承受紧缩金融条件带来的估值压力，AI投资可持续性的疑虑也将难以消散。 对于未来市场走向，Matsuzawa维持此前的核心预测不变： 在美联储政策真正转向之前，全球科技股难以走出实质性的系统性反弹。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 村田五年豪掷1万亿日元扩产MLCC
articles.summary: 日本村田制作所将在五年内投资 1 万亿日元（63 亿美元），以满足其人工智能服务器和设备尖端电子元件日益增长的需求。 村田制作所周五公布的投资计划旨在提高多层陶瓷电容器（MLCC）的供应能力，以满足当前人工智能服务器的需求，并为未来人工智能设备的普及做好准备。该公司每年将投入约2000亿日元，约为此前投入的两倍。 村田制作所社长中岛纪夫在周五的财报电话会议上表示：“我们决定投资的最大原因是MLCC（多层陶瓷电容器）供应不足，无法满足数据中心的需求。” MLCC用于稳定电流，是所有电子设备中不可或缺的元件。 一台人工智能服务器需要使用15000到25000个MLCC（多层陶瓷电容器），大约是智能手机所需数量的10倍。随着全球数据中心建设的蓬勃发展，对MLCC的需求正在激增。 用于人工智能服务器的MLCC（多层陶瓷电容器）面临着额外的技术挑战。据中岛介绍，村田制作所在全球MLCC市场占有40%的份额，在用于人工智能服务器的先进产品市场占有超过50%的份额。该公司工厂的利用率一直保持在95%左右。 约3500亿日元将用于建筑项目，其中包括1500亿日元用于在日本西部冈山县建设两座新的多层陶瓷电容器（MLCC）和陶瓷原料生产厂，预计分别于2028年和2030年竣工。村田制作所还将在附近的岛根县建设一座新工厂。 该公司还将加强其海外生产基地，包括计划于 2030 年在其泰国工厂增建一座新厂房。此外，还将在其菲律宾工厂的闲置区域安装新的生产设备。 剩余的6500亿日元将用于日本、中国和东盟国家现有工厂的生产设备。通过这项投资，该公司计划到2031年3月结束的财年，将多层陶瓷电容器（MLCC）的销售额从2026年3月结束的财年的9000亿日元提高一倍以上。 受MLCC（多层陶瓷电容器）市场繁荣的推动，村田制作所的盈利表现稳健。该公司周五预测，截至2027年3月的财年，其合并净利润将同比增长69%，达到3960亿日元。此次上调预期，在原本已预计创下利润新纪录的基础上，又增加了580亿日元。根据QUICK Consensus的数据，这一预期高于近期市场平均预测值3689亿日元。 预计全年营收将增长23%至2.26万亿日元，营业利润将增长85%至5200亿日元，两项数据均创历史新高，分别较上调预期上调了1500亿日元和900亿日元。截至9月份的季度，村田制作所的订单出货比为1.28，高于1的阈值，表明市场需求强劲。 该公司此次资本投资旨在满足近期数据中心的需求，同时也满足中长期设备组件的需求。“从2030年开始，随着数据中心投资增速放缓，边缘设备和人形机器人的需求将会扩大，电子元件市场也将随之增长。”中岛表示。 随着终端产品日趋复杂，每个设备所需的元件数量也随之增加，因此对更小巧、高性能元件的需求预计将会攀升。该公司认为，MLCC产能的扩大在机器人等新兴领域将具有重要价值。 然而，一些分析师对人工智能热潮的可持续性表示质疑。随着美国超大规模数据中心运营商在数据中心投入巨资，人们越来越担心过度投资会导致财务负担加重，尤其是在利率上升使得融资成本更高的情况下。 文章来源： 半导体行业观察 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
